_about: Source of truth for the podcast. tools/build-podcast.py turns it into podcast/feed.xml, the chapter files, the episode list on /insights/podcast/ and the podcast section of each article. The feed URL must never change once the show is listed in Apple Podcasts and Spotify.

show._feed_public: false = the podcast is only on the website: no feed.xml, no RSS links. true = feed.xml is published for Apple Podcasts, Spotify & co. Rebuild after changing it.
show.title: Insights with Martin Motlík
show.author: Martin Motlík
show.description: A podcast that takes the ideas from Martin Motlík's Insights articles into conversation. With a background in construction and a career in digital strategy, Martin explores how the web, communication and AI are changing the AEC industry. Together with Sarah, his virtual AI co-host, he discusses what these changes mean in practice, one article and one practical case per episode. Both voices are made with AI: Martin's is an AI clone of his own voice, and Sarah is a fictional co-host.
show._topics: What the show is about: JSON-LD "about" and "keywords" on the podcast page.
show._cover: Cover files carry a version (-v2): podcast apps and social networks cache artwork by URL, so a changed cover needs a new file name. Bump it with every redesign; tools/podcast-covers.mjs writes the files.
show._subscribe_endpoint: Form endpoint for "Get new episodes" (Formspree: https://formspree.io/f/<id>). Empty = the button and form are left out.
show._stats_prefix: Analytics prefix put in front of the MP3 URL in feed.xml (OP3: free, open, no personal data; stats at https://op3.dev/show/<podcast:guid>). Apps download through it and it redirects to the file. The website player plays the file directly. Empty = plain URLs.
show._platforms: Where the show is listed: buttons in the podcast page hero and sameAs in the PodcastSeries JSON-LD. The Apple link has no country, so Apple opens the visitor's own store.

episodes.title: Be the source: getting AEC data ready for AI search
episodes.hero_alt: Martin Motlík working on a laptop outdoors, surrounded by the icons of AI assistants and search engines
episodes.teaser: Sarah runs marketing at a structural engineering firm in Portland. Her firm ranks on page one, yet ChatGPT named five others. Martin takes her situation apart, from project galleries and PDFs to the load path of a fact.
episodes.summary: Sarah runs marketing at a structural engineering firm in Portland. Her firm ranks on page one, yet when she asked ChatGPT which local firms have real mass-timber experience, it named five others. Martin takes her situation apart: why page one is no longer the finish line, how project galleries and PDFs hide the facts engineers search for, what localizing a timber page for U.S. and Canadian design codes taught him, and how a fact travels the “load path” into an AI answer.

episodes.disclosure: Martin's voice is an AI clone of his own voice; Sarah is a fictional co-host voiced by AI. Produced with ElevenLabs.

episodes.title: A power outlet for AI: what MCP means for AEC
episodes.hero_alt: ChatGPT's answer comparing revisions R02 and R03 of a residential building, next to a web-based 3D viewer of revision R03: the three doors on Residential Level 3 that still lack a fire rating are red, the building services are colored by system, and the Checks panel shows 13 of 14 requirements passed.
episodes.teaser: Sarah’s boss forwarded a vendor email: “Should we be doing this MCP thing?” Martin walks her through his own IFC model-review test, from thirteen failing elements to three doors highlighted in the model, and what still needs human judgment.
episodes.summary: An AI answer about a building model is only useful if you can check it. Martin walks through his IFC model-review test, explains where MCP helps, and shows what still needs human judgment. See the screenshots and tool details in the companion article.
